title: Longer than a mayfly's whole grown-up life
detail: Most adult mayflies live less than a day. You made it through a full one.

title: More than two days on Jupiter
detail: Jupiter spins so fast that one of its days lasts about 10 hours.

title: About 100,000 heartbeats
detail: Your heart beats roughly 100,000 times a day. Every one of them today was a sober one.

title: Longer than Lindbergh's flight across the Atlantic
detail: Charles Lindbergh flew nonstop from New York to Paris in 1927 in about 33½ hours.

title: Long enough to fly to the Moon
detail: Apollo 11 took about three days to get from Earth to the Moon.

title: Longer than Apollo 13's trip
detail: The crew of Apollo 13 made it home safely after just under six days, against the odds.

title: About 11 million miles around the Sun
detail: The Earth carries you about 1.6 million miles along its orbit every day.

title: Longer than the whole Apollo 11 mission
detail: In July 1969 the crew flew to the Moon, walked on it and came home in 8 days and 3 hours.

title: Double digits
detail: Ten days in a row.

title: About a million heartbeats
detail: At roughly 100,000 beats a day, your heart has beaten about a million times since day one.

title: As long as the longest nonstop bird flight
detail: In 2022 a young bar-tailed godwit flew from Alaska to Tasmania in 11 days without landing once.

title: As long as a robin's eggs take to hatch
detail: American robin eggs hatch in about two weeks.

title: As long as the Thai cave rescue
detail: In 2018 a youth soccer team and their coach were trapped in a flooded cave for 17 days. All 13 came out alive.

title: As long as it takes a chick to hatch
detail: A chicken egg takes 21 days to hatch.

title: As long as the Tour de France
detail: The race takes about three weeks, with two rest days. You didn't get any rest days.

title: The Sun has turned all the way around
detail: At its equator, the Sun spins once about every 25 days.

title: The Moon has gone all the way around the Earth
detail: One trip around takes the Moon about 27⅓ days.

title: Longer than a housefly's whole life
detail: Most houseflies live about four weeks.

title: About a whole new outer layer of skin
detail: The outer layer of your skin renews itself roughly every four weeks.

title: A full cycle of the Moon's phases
detail: New moon to new moon takes about 29½ days.

title: As long as the James Webb telescope's trip
detail: The space telescope launched on Christmas Day 2021 and reached its post, a million miles from Earth, 30 days later.

title: As long as a rabbit's pregnancy
detail: Baby rabbits are born about 31 days after they're conceived.

title: More than 1,000 hours
detail: Six weeks is 1,008 hours, each one lived one at a time.

title: Roughly a million breaths
detail: You breathe about 20,000 times a day, every one of them one at a time.

title: Longer than one day on Mercury
detail: Mercury spins so slowly that one turn takes about 59 Earth days.

title: As long as sea turtle eggs take to hatch
detail: Sea turtle eggs stay buried in warm sand for about two months before the hatchlings dig out.

title: As long as it takes for puppies and kittens to be born
detail: Dogs and cats are both pregnant for about nine weeks.

title: Longer than the first drive across America
detail: In 1903 Horatio Nelson Jackson drove a car from San Francisco to New York in 63 days, on roads that were mostly dirt.

title: As long as an emperor penguin dad keeps watch
detail: Emperor penguin fathers hold their egg on their feet through the Antarctic winter for about 65 days, without eating.

title: As long as the Chilean miners waited
detail: In 2010, 33 miners were trapped deep underground for 69 days. Every one of them was brought up alive.

title: 100,000 minutes
detail: A hundred thousand minutes, one at a time.

title: As long as Nellie Bly's trip around the world
detail: In 1889 the reporter Nellie Bly circled the globe in 72 days, beating the fictional record of 80.

title: Around the world in 80 days
detail: As long as the trip in Jules Verne's 1872 novel.

title: As long as the Skylab 4 mission
detail: In 1973 and 1974 three astronauts lived aboard the Skylab space station for 84 days.

title: A whole year on Mercury
detail: Mercury goes around the Sun every 88 days.

title: A Fibonacci number
detail: 89 is in the Fibonacci sequence, the numbers that show up in the spirals of sunflowers and pinecones.

title: As long as the Opportunity rover was built to last
detail: NASA planned for about 90 days on Mars. Opportunity kept going for almost 15 years, one day at a time.

title: As long as Sputnik 1 stayed in orbit
detail: The first satellite circled the Earth for 92 days, from October 1957 to January 1958.

title: As long as Amundsen's trip to the South Pole and back
detail: In 1911 Roald Amundsen's team skied to the South Pole and back to their base in just over three months.

title: Triple digits
detail: 100 days in a row.

title: As long as the Kon-Tiki voyage
detail: In 1947 six men sailed a balsa-wood raft 4,300 miles across the Pacific in 101 days.

title: As long as a lion's pregnancy
detail: Lion cubs are born after about 110 days.

title: As long as a pig's pregnancy
detail: Farmers say it's three months, three weeks and three days: 114 days.

title: Ten million seconds
detail: Ten million seconds, give or take a few thousand.

title: A whole new set of red blood cells
detail: Red blood cells live about 120 days, so nearly every one in your body has been made since you got here.

title: As long as Shackleton's men waited for rescue
detail: In 1916, 22 men waited on Antarctica's Elephant Island for 137 days. All of them were saved.

title: A gross of days
detail: Twelve dozen days.

title: A Fibonacci number
detail: 144 is in the Fibonacci sequence, and it's also 12 times 12.

title: As long as a sheep's pregnancy
detail: Lambs are born after about five months.

title: 200 days
detail: Two hundred days in a row.

title: As long as the Perseverance rover's trip to Mars
detail: NASA's rover launched on July 30, 2020 and landed on Mars 203 days later.

title: A whole year on Venus
detail: Venus goes around the Sun every 225 Earth days.

title: A Fibonacci number
detail: 233 is in the Fibonacci sequence, the numbers behind sunflower spirals.

title: One day on Venus
detail: Venus takes 243 Earth days to spin once, so its day is longer than its year.

title: 250 days
detail: A quarter of the way to a thousand.

title: 256 days
detail: Two to the eighth power, a very round number to a computer.

title: As long as a cow's pregnancy
detail: Calves are born after about 283 days.

title: As long as a swift can stay in the air
detail: Common swifts can fly for up to 10 months without landing.

title: 300 days
detail: Three hundred days in a row.

title: Pi days
detail: 314 days, like 3.14.

title: 333 days
detail: All threes.

title: Longer than a blue whale's pregnancy
detail: A blue whale calf grows for about 11 months before it's born, already about 23 feet long.

title: As long as Scott Kelly's year in space
detail: Astronaut Scott Kelly spent 340 days aboard the International Space Station in 2015 and 2016.

title: As long as a horse's pregnancy
detail: Foals are born after about 11 months.

title: About six inches of hair
detail: Hair grows about half an inch a month, so yours has grown about six inches since day one.

title: A Fibonacci number
detail: 377 is in the Fibonacci sequence.

title: 400 days
detail: Four hundred days in a row.

title: As long as it took to build the Empire State Building
detail: Work began on March 17, 1930, and it opened 410 days later, on May 1, 1931.

title: More than 10,000 hours
detail: The number of hours often said to make someone an expert. You're getting good at this.

title: Longer than anyone has stayed in space in one trip
detail: Cosmonaut Valeri Polyakov spent about 437 days aboard the Mir space station in 1994 and 1995, the longest single spaceflight on record.

title: 444 days
detail: All fours.

title: Longer than a giraffe's pregnancy
detail: Giraffes carry their calves for about 15 months. Newborns arrive with a fall of about five feet, then stand up within an hour.

title: 500 days
detail: Halfway to a thousand.

title: 512 days
detail: Two to the ninth power.

title: As long as Voyager 1's trip to Jupiter
detail: Voyager 1 launched on September 5, 1977 and flew past Jupiter 546 days later.

title: 555 days
detail: All fives.

title: As long as the Pony Express ran
detail: Riders carried the mail across the American West from April 1860 to October 1861, about 19 months.

title: 600 days

title: A Fibonacci number
detail: 610 is in the Fibonacci sequence.

title: Longer than an elephant's pregnancy
detail: African elephants carry their calves for about 22 months, the longest of any land animal.

title: A whole year on Mars
detail: Mars takes 687 Earth days to go around the Sun.

title: A million minutes
detail: One million minutes, give or take a few.

title: 100 weeks

title: 777 days
detail: All sevens. Lucky.

title: 800 days

title: As long as the first voyage around the world
detail: Magellan's fleet left Spain in September 1519. One ship, led by Juan Sebastián Elcano, made it home in September 1522.

detail: All ones. Make a wish.

detail: A hundred million seconds.
